title: CVForge application dossier
description: Everything about an application that is NOT the letter: what the job is, how you pitched yourself, the posting, who you spoke to, where it stands. Never committed - recruiter contacts are someone else's personal data and a posting is someone else's copyrighted text. No renderer reads this file. `cvforge list` does, to find earlier applications like a new one; `cvforge check` validates it. Title, language, reference and attachments are not repeated here: they are in letter.yaml.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what the job is - the domain, the problem, the stack. The anchor for finding similar applications later, so write what makes this job this job, not what every posting says. E.g. 'Python perception for warehouse robots: bin picking from RGB-D cameras, ROS 2, on-device inference.'

keywords.description: Free keywords for similarity: domain and technology, lowercase, English, singular. E.g. [robotics, bin picking, python, ros, edge deployment]. No fixed vocabulary - reuse a word you used before where it fits, so `cvforge list --match` finds both.

name.description: How you refer to the company, e.g. 'ACME Robotics Lab Berlin'. Omit to use letter.yaml's recipient.company, which is the legal entity.

about.description: Two or three sentences on the company: what it makes, size, where.

title.description: The job title - only for an application without a letter.yaml, e.g. one built before CVForge. Otherwise the letter's job.title is the one used.

location.description: Where the job is, as the posting says it.

applied.description: The day you submitted, "YYYY-MM-DD". null while it is a draft. Set it together with `status: applied` - `cvforge check` warns when the two disagree.

fetched.description: When you archived it, "YYYY-MM-DD". Postings are taken down; this dates the copy in posting/.

archive.description: The archived posting, relative to this application's directory, e.g. posting/posting.pdf - the same rule as a one-off attachment, so the path survives the application moving. Print to PDF rather than screenshot: it keeps the text selectable and the whole posting, not one viewport of it.

notes.description: What the posting actually asks for, in your own words. The requirements worth answering in the letter.

approach.description: How you pitched yourself. The part worth reusing: what to lead with for a job like this one.

based_on.description: Slug of the earlier application this one started from, if any - its letter or CV structure.

angle.description: What the letter leads with and argues - the hook, and the experience it puts first.

cv.description: The tailoring in short, one item per change: 'flagship project first in projects', 'theses removed', 'skill group Robotics added'.

gaps.description: Where you fall short of the posting, and how the letter handles it.

url.description: The application link, if it is not posting.url.

questions.description: What the portal asks besides the documents, and your answer.

contacts.description: Recruiters, hiring managers, anyone you spoke to.

timeline.description: What happened when. Free-form entries, newest last.
